purpose: Per CEO R291 P2: 'Do not merely cite VIEshunt. Create a VIEshunt comparison matrix. VIEshunt's published 24-hour hardware-in-loop testing makes this an especially important benchmark.'
source: VIEshunt: towards a ventricular intelligent and electromechanical shunt for hydrocephalus therapy. PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40087797/

Both are closed-loop. P-01 adds BOUNDED RATE of conductance change.

vieshunt_comparison_matrix.p_01: TBD (not yet tested — added to R291 physiological disturbances)
vieshunt_comparison_matrix.differentiation: VIEshunt has demonstrated posture adaptation. P-01 has NOT. This is a gap to close.

vieshunt_comparison_matrix.p_01: ✅ (2%/sec bounded rate, confirmed critical by 225-run ablation)
vieshunt_comparison_matrix.differentiation: P-01's CORE MECHANISM. VIEshunt does not appear to use rate-limited control. This is P-01's primary technical differentiator.
P-01 uses multiple parallel drainage paths. VIEshunt appears to use a single path. This is a structural difference.

vieshunt_comparison_matrix.differentiation: P-01 has explicit sensor-health detector + safe fallback. US20260115436A1 also covers this, so it's not a unique differentiator, but P-01's implementation is specific.

vieshunt_comparison_matrix.vieshunt: Published (24h HIL test with ICP, abdominal pressure, posture)
vieshunt_comparison_matrix.p_01: Computational benchmark (225-run ablation, 9 attack modes). Physical benchmark PENDING.
vieshunt_comparison_matrix.differentiation: VIEshunt has PHYSICAL evidence. P-01 has COMPUTATIONAL evidence only. This is P-01's biggest gap vs VIEshunt.

vieshunt_comparison_matrix.p_01: PLANNED (80-run blinded bench protocol, BOM ready, not yet built)
vieshunt_comparison_matrix.differentiation: VIEshunt has built and tested hardware. P-01 has not. Closing this gap is the #1 priority.
VIEshunt has animal data. P-01 does not. This is a multi-year gap.
VIEshunt has wireless. P-01's bench prototype is wired. Wireless is an implantable-version concern.
VIEshunt has IMU for posture detection. P-01 does not. This is a gap for posture adaptation.

the_key_question: What does P-01's bounded-rate control add beyond what VIEshunt already demonstrates?

the_answer.vieshunt_has: Hardware (micro-pump, flow meter, pressure sensor, IMU, wireless, microcontroller) + physical HIL test + animal pilot + posture adaptation
the_answer.p_01_has: Control algorithm (bounded-rate conductance control + multi-segment redistribution + sensor-health fallback) + 225-run computational ablation confirming rate limiting as dominant mechanism + 180-run comparison showing 2-3x advantage over existing closed-loop
the_answer.the_differentiator: VIEshunt has the HARDWARE. P-01 has the ALGORITHM. Specifically: VIEshunt does not appear to use bounded-rate conductance control or multi-segment redistribution. P-01's computational evidence shows these produce a 2-3x robustness advantage. The physical bench must confirm whether this advantage survives outside the simulator.
the_answer.the_gap: VIEshunt has physical evidence (HIL test, animal pilot). P-01 has computational evidence only. Closing this gap is the #1 priority. The 80-run blinded bench protocol is designed to do exactly this.
the_answer.commercial_position: P-01 is NOT competing with VIEshunt on hardware. P-01 is offering a CONTROL ALGORITHM that could potentially be applied to VIEshunt's hardware (or any similar intelligent shunt platform). The buyer question is: 'Does adding bounded-rate conductance control to your existing hardware produce a measurable robustness advantage?'

buyer_facing_statement: VIEshunt (2025) has demonstrated an intelligent electromechanical shunt with hardware-in-loop testing and animal pilot. P-01 is NOT a competing hardware platform. P-01 is a CONTROL ALGORITHM (bounded-rate conductance control) that could be applied to any intelligent shunt hardware, including VIEshunt-class systems. Our computational evidence (225-run ablation) shows the rate-limiting mechanism produces a 2-3x robustness advantage. The physical bench is designed to determine whether that advantage survives outside the simulator. If it does, the algorithm could potentially improve any existing intelligent shunt — including VIEshunt.
